script: Don't think of a white bear. Don't. Too late, right? In nineteen eighty-seven, psychologist Daniel Wegner tried this on students. They talked out loud for five minutes. One rule. Don't think of a white bear. Every time it popped up, they rang a bell. Ding. Ding. Ding. And when the rule ended, the bear came back even more. Fighting a thought keeps it alive. Same with an ex. Or that awkward thing you said. But one trick helped. Pick a different thought on purpose. In the study, it was a red car. So picture a red car. And whatever you do, don't think of a white bear.
